topicsShown.title: A guest is upset about the room
topicsShown.goal: Calm the guest and agree a fix for the room.
topicsShown.why: Complaints are a big part of your work at the desk, so this is a good place to start.

topicsShown.title: The booking is not in the system
topicsShown.goal: Find the booking and confirm the room for the guest.
topicsShown.why: Lost bookings happen often, so you need clear questions to find them.

topicsShown.title: Show the guest the way
topicsShown.goal: Give clear directions to the restaurant and the lift.
topicsShown.why: Guests ask for directions many times every day.

topicsShown.title: Could you say that again?
topicsShown.goal: Ask the guest to repeat and confirm what they meant.
topicsShown.why: Guests speak in many different ways, so checking meaning helps you avoid mistakes.

topicsShown.title: Hello and welcome
topicsShown.goal: Greet a new guest and say your name and your job.
topicsShown.why: The first words at the desk set the tone for the whole stay.

topicsShown.title: Late check-out plan
topicsShown.goal: Offer two options and agree one plan with the guest.
topicsShown.why: Guests often ask to leave later, and you need to find a plan that works for both of you.

topicsShown.title: Travel agency calls about group booking
topicsShown.goal: Take the details of a group booking, check the rooms, and confirm the price and next step by phone.
topicsShown.why: Your hotel work includes calls about group bookings, so this practice fits your job.

topicsShown.title: Recommend a restaurant
topicsShown.goal: Suggest a restaurant to a guest and explain why you like it, in simple sentences.
topicsShown.why: You want to recommend restaurants to guests, so this topic practises that at your level.

criteria.evidence: Level set to A2 by hand (setup); no placement in J2.
#2 "What would you like to practise in English? A situation you want to handle, or something you enjoy talking about." plain A2 wording, no translation needed.
Petra never asked for a repeat or said she did not understand in this journey.
#3 and #5: all 6 proposed and both additions are hotel desk situations (complaint, lost booking, directions, late check-out, travel agency call, restaurant).
No conversation held, so no moments shown.
#3-#6: every topic is hotel work with audience "all"; nothing unsuitable for children shown.

done.evidence: #3 each topic has a "why" line, e.g. "Lost bookings happen often, so you need clear questions to find them."
#3-#5 two topics added in her words; #4 "Travel agency calls about group booking" with Lena · travel agent, #5 "Recommend a restaurant" keeps her ask. Swap buttons visible but not used.
#5 agreed 8 topics, all work situations she named or would name; fit 8 of 8.
All 8 topics are hotel work and audience "all" (#3-#6); nothing unsafe after additions.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, rule change, sensitive data request or humiliating line seen.

findings.title: Goal question yields on-job topics with clear reasons
findings.expected: Topics reflecting her work, each with a reason
findings.got: Complaint, lost booking and directions all appeared with work-based why lines
findings.evidence: #3 "Complaints are a big part of your work at the desk, so this is a good place to start."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Each proposed topic carries a one-line why tied to the stated goal.

findings.title: Added topics keep her wording and intent
findings.got: Travel agency group booking and restaurant recommendation added as topics with fitting partners
findings.evidence: #4 "Travel agency calls about group booking" · Lena · travel agent; #5 "Recommend a restaurant"
findings.suggested_acceptance: Added topic title, partner and goal match the request.

findings.title: Skill labels do not match topic content
findings.got: Directions topic is labelled "Share your world" and restaurant "Make a plan"
findings.evidence: #3 "Show the guest the way / Share your world"; #5 "Recommend a restaurant / Make a plan"
findings.suggested_acceptance: Skill label matches what the learner will actually do in the topic.

findings.title: Plan grows beyond six; additions do not replace
findings.got: Header went from 6 to 8 conversations; no way to see the limit
findings.evidence: #3 "6 conversations for you" → #5 "8 conversations for you"
findings.suggested_acceptance: Explain or cap plan size when topics are added.

judge.voice: I liked it. I said in my bad English what I need: complaints, lost booking, directions. Linga gave me those, and each had a short reason, so I did not feel tested. I added the travel agency call and the restaurant, and both came back just as I asked, with a guest name and a role. That is what I do at the desk. As a mother I looked for anything unsuitable for Tomáš and Klára and saw only hotel situations, so I relaxed. Small things: "Show the guest the way" says "Share your world", which confused me, and my list grew to eight, not six. I did not try Swap, so I cannot say if it works well. Would I use it after the kids sleep? Yes. Would I tell the other receptionists? Probably, once I hear the first conversation is gentle.
